body.statement:
For the concrete input \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1)=\varnothing\), while \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1,0,1)=\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}})\) and
\[
 F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)=P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0))
\]
for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\).  Hence the certified partial procedure has a successful query outside the defined generic front-door family.  No universal inclusion of that family, Assaad-certificate embedding, or general certificate-indexed functional is asserted.
body.justification: The concrete outside-family success is proved directly.
body.gap: Universal front-door-family inclusion and Assaad embedding are removed.
body.consumer: The witness remains an executable positive regression test.
body.proof_tex:
For \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), the coordinate set is \(V=\{X,Y\}\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def:micro\text{-}frontdoor\text{-}family}\) requires a nonempty set
\[
 \mathcal D\subseteq(V\setminus\{X,Y\})\times[-b,0].
\]
The right side is empty, so \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1)=\varnothing\).  By the first ordered branch of \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\), the procedure returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}})\) on this exact input.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:outside\text{-}witness\text{-}identification}\) gives, for every compatible \(M\),
\[
 F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)
 =P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0)).
\]
Thus the certified procedure has a successful input outside the defined front-door family.  The proof neither maps every certificate to a transducer trace nor claims that Assaad's published criterion is embedded; those parts of the former statement required an unspecified \(F_c\) and unspecified transitions and have been removed.
